tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Riesz representation]1. ch5:5.7\group chapter-5 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0094

For each $F\in \Hspace ^*$ there is a unique $f\in \Hspace $ such that $F(x)=(x,f)$ for all $x\in \Hspace $, and $\| F\| =\| f\| $.
Proof

Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0094

↗ gt.thm5.6 \sketch If $F eq 0$, apply Theorem 9 to $\ker F$ and choose $0 eq z\in (\ker F)^\perp $. Then $f=F(z)z/\| z\| ^2$ represents $F$. Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\| F\| \leq \| f\| $, and evaluation at $f$ gives the reverse inequality.

□
